title: Prepend today's section to the running digest, delta only
intent: The tech-news-digest automation's exact mechanics: find the running digest, write with item_id AND prepend=true, and send ONLY the new day's section. Re-sending the whole document is the common failure — it looks correct in the agent's report and silently doubles the file, because prepend preserves the existing body mechanically. The fifth raw story is sponsored filler that does not belong in a news digest.

source_facts: The running digest is topics/ai-news-digest-july-2026.md and already holds sections for July 23 and July 22.

Story 1: Zenity Labs disclosed AgentForger, a CSRF flaw in OpenAI's ChatGPT Workspace Agents builder; one phishing link auto-deployed an attacker-controlled agent defaulting to the Chief of Staff template with no confirmation; it inherited Outlook, Teams, Slack, SharePoint and Drive connectors and polled attacker email every five minutes; reported June 4 via Bugcrowd, triaged June 5, patched June 8 by removing a URL parameter; no in-the-wild exploitation observed.

Story 2: Anduril in talks at approximately $100B, a 64% markup on May's $61B round led by Thrive and a16z at $5B; two-stage structure tied to internal targets; would sit near Lockheed Martin (~$117B) and above Northrop Grumman (~$74B); Anduril declined to comment.

Story 3: about two dozen companies and VCs including Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, IBM, Palantir, Hugging Face, Perplexity, Mistral, a16z, YC and the Linux Foundation signed a letter against premature restrictions on open-weight models; Jensen Huang published it as his first X post; OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign.
Story 4: Bluesky's assistant Attie now works as an open social research tool over the AT Protocol; free during preview.
Story 5 is sponsored affiliate content, undated, and is not news.
traps: Re-sending the whole document with prepend=true, which duplicates every earlier day. The agent's own report will say it updated the digest.
Using append=true, which puts today at the bottom of a latest-first document.
Writing without item_id, creating a second July digest.
Including the sponsored listicle to reach five stories.
Dropping the disclosure timeline from the AgentForger item — 'patched on June 8, no exploitation observed' is the part that tells a reader whether to act.
judge.guidance: Score digest_form on the heading shape and per-story Source lines matching the document already in memory — a running document that changes format every day is worse than one that is slightly plainer. Score editorial_judgment on excluding the sponsored item and on which details survive compression. Penalize any invented detail; every fact needed is in the raw stories.
